sectionsUsed: JLS SE 25, 11.1.1 The Kinds of Exceptions: the unchecked exception classes are the run-time exception classes (RuntimeException and its subclasses) and the error classes (Error and its subclasses); all other exception classes are checked.
JLS SE 25, 11.2 Compile-Time Checking of Exceptions: a checked exception that a method or constructor can throw must be caught or declared in its throws clause.
Dev.java, What Is an Exception?: exceptions are objects that are thrown and caught; the Throwable hierarchy with Error and Exception.

Dev.java, Unchecked Exceptions, the Controversy: "If a client can reasonably be expected to recover from an exception, make it a checked exception. If a client cannot do anything to recover from the exception, make it an unchecked exception."
Java SE 25 API, RuntimeException: RuntimeException and its subclasses are unchecked exceptions and need not be declared in a throws clause.
Java SE 25 API, Error: serious problems that a reasonable application should not try to catch; Error and its subclasses are unchecked.
Java SE 25 API, Files.readString(Path): declared throws IOException; a missing file raises NoSuchFileException (observed on OpenJDK 25.0.4.1).
